sections.title: Knowledge & Dialogue Across the Arts & Sciences (PD)
sections.description: COLL 2000 extends student experiences in the first-year Kite and Key courses. Students in the COLL 2000 reflect upon, theorize, and integrate the different epistemologies of the humanities, arts, natural sciences, and social sciences. Students will experience, and learn to facilitate, inclusive, evidence-informed learning environments that promote student success through dialogue, mentorship, collaboration, active learning, and reflective practice. Topics include: knowledge production in higher education; interdisciplinary and collaborative inquiry; the role and practice of dialogue and active learning strategies; and peer mentoring and advising. Attendance and active listening and participation are required. Other assignments may include writing assignments, projects, field trips, in class activities, and classroom simulations and observations. The goal of the COLL 2000 is to cultivate a cohort of College peer mentors, learning facilitators, and leaders who can guide incoming first-year students and foster engagement with the curiosity-driven education that the College of Arts & Sciences provides. Students will leave the course having assembled their own toolkit of ideas and practices related to knowledge, inquiry, and dialogue that is relevant to their values and meaningful for the kinds of scholarly, community-based, professional, or personal work they are committed to. Students who complete COLL 2000 will be eligible to serve as College Fellows for future Kite and Key courses. This is an SNF Paideia-designated course and is open to all Penn students, not just Paideia fellows.
